title: Event-Driven Architecture
description: Implement event-driven systems with message brokers, event sourcing, CQRS, and handle eventual consistency in distributed environments.

data.text: Event-driven architecture decouples services through events. Services emit events when state changes, and other services react to those events. This enables loose coupling and scalability.

data.text: Message brokers (RabbitMQ, Azure Service Bus, Kafka) provide reliable message delivery, routing, and durability. Choose based on throughput requirements, ordering needs, and infrastructure.

data.title: Event Publishing with MassTransit

data.text: Event sourcing stores all state changes as events. CQRS separates read and write models. Together, they provide auditability, temporal queries, and optimized read/write paths.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Event-driven architecture decouples services through asynchronous events
Message brokers provide reliable, durable message delivery
Events should be immutable and represent facts that occurred
Event sourcing stores state changes as an event log
CQRS separates read and write models for optimization
Eventual consistency is inherent in event-driven systems
Idempotent consumers are essential for handling duplicate messages
data.takeaway: Event-driven architecture enables loose coupling and scalability. Use message brokers for reliable delivery, event sourcing for auditability, and CQRS for optimized read/write paths. Embrace eventual consistency.
